newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRIVATISATION NO PANACEA FOR S.AFRICA - MARCUS.
newsitem.headline: PRIVATISATION NO PANACEA FOR S.AFRICA - MARCUS.

text.p: Privatisation should not be seen as a panacea for all South Africa's inherited social and economic imbalances, Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus said on Wednesday.

"It is widely recognised that government alone cannot bear the entire responsibility of providing housing, infrastructure and other basic services," Marcus said in a mini-debate in the national assembly.
"Therefore government, particularly in relation to local needs, is looking at public-private sector partnerships in the provision of basic services.
"This is not seen simply as a panacea for all ills but as a way of building partnerships to enable different sectors to gain access to a wider range of services, skills and resources."
But partnerships needed sound government intervention and involvement, particularly when dealing with the poor who did not have the market power of the private sector.
"Government must and does take account of the fact that while the private sector is primarily motived by financial returns on investment, it has a far greater responsibility," she said.
"Therefore our approach includes government allocating resources and harnessing the resources of the parastatals as a key means to help address the inequities of our society."
Government's role was to ensure the right environment for restructuring, including privatisation and partnerships to take place.

"This means providing the appropriate legal, fiscal and regulatory framework required to galvanise the resources needed to meet the demand. We are looking at restructuring state assets, not simply privatisation, aggressive or otherwise."
The proceeds of privatisation would be used to retire state debt, expand services, ensure technological and skills transfer or a combination of any of these.
A concrete example of this had been the sale of a percentage of Telkom to a strategic equity partner.
